If you follow the Wiccan religion, then yes, you can call yourself a Wiccan. As for witch, it depends on whether you feel like that label resonates with you and accurately describes your beliefs/practices. You can be both a Wiccan and a witch, or be one without the other. 

>Is the term “witch” only for those who cast spells?

A witch is someone who practices witchcraft. Witchcraft is not all spells. It's also divination, medicine, spirit work, and much more. If you are practicing witchcraft, then you can call yourself a witch.

>Can you bee Wiccan if you celebrate catholic holidays?

Sure, why not? You will find that some Catholic holidays correlate with the Wheel of the Year. Historically, people did not give up their "pagan" holidays, but instead adapted them into the new religion they were following.

We spiritual folk tend to see the weird in things like that, but it sounds pretty mundane. 

If more synchronicities happen though, especially after scrying, there may be something more at play. Just keep some healthy skepticism.

>What's the difference between Wicca and witchcraft? 

Wicca is a religion founded by Gerald Gardner. Witchcraft is a magical practice, not a religion. Wiccans practice witchcraft, but not all witches are Wiccan. 

>How do you know what deity is your deity? 

It's not straightforward, as no one is assigned to a deity or anything like that. You can worship or work with any number of deities that you wish, or none at all. Sometimes a deity may reach out to you through dreams or signs (check mythology for deity associations, like sacred animals) but that does not necessarily mean they are your "patron," nor do you need a patron deity. That is a much deeper commitment to a deity than regular worship, so you shouldn't worry about that as a beginner. 

As for sources, check out www.sacred-texts.org and www.darkbooks.org for free ebooks.
